final.memo:
The Company is currently undergoing a Chapter 11 bankruptcy restructuring following a catastrophic collapse in travel demand [D03]. Despite the clear insolvency of the business, the stock is currently trading at a nonsensical price of $5.53, driven by retail speculation regarding a potential recovery [D04]. This disconnect between market pricing and fundamental reality represents a classic short opportunity for those who understand the mechanics of bankruptcy.

With total debt ballooning to approximately $18.8 billion against an asset base whose value has been significantly impaired, it is mathematically certain that there is no residual value for common equity holders [D04], [D05]. In any standard recovery waterfall, creditors must be made whole before a single cent reaches the equity, and the current debt load precludes this outcome by a wide margin [D05]. While peers like AMERCO maintain healthy margins of 13.6%, this company is facing a terminal decline in its core rental segments [D06].

The market’s current infatuation with the stock as a 'reopening trade' is fundamentally flawed [D01]. We anticipate that the bankruptcy court process will swiftly dismantle this narrative as it enforces the absolute priority rule, leaving common shareholders with nothing [D03], [D05]. Administrative expenses and the inevitable losses from forced fleet liquidations will only further erode any potential asset coverage that might theoretically exist [D05].

Our role is to capture the value destruction as the market eventually aligns with the reality of the bankruptcy court process [D03]. We are entering this position with a 2% target size, acknowledging the risk of retail-driven volatility and potential short squeezes [D04], [D05]. We will maintain this position until the court-supervised proceedings confirm our thesis or the structural risks reach our predefined kill criteria [D05].
